title: How Do You Source Hard-to-Find or Discontinued Semiconductor Components?
text:
K

Kieu
New member

As semiconductor supply chains become more complex, finding the right component is not always a matter of checking distributor stock.

Engineers and procurement teams may eventually face situations such as:

A critical IC has been discontinued or is approaching EOL
Authorized distributors have no available stock
Lead times are too long for an urgent production requirement
A specific manufacturer part number is difficult to source
Excess inventory is available in one region but difficult to access from another
A replacement part requires careful technical and supply-chain evaluation
I'm curious how other engineers and procurement professionals handle these situations.

Do you typically work with authorized distributors, independent distributors, broker networks, or specialized sourcing companies?

One company I have been looking into is Lovechip, an international electronic component sourcing company focused on semiconductors and hard-to-find components.

Their sourcing service covers components such as MCUs, memory, power management ICs, FPGA, sensors, MOSFETs, and other semiconductor devices. They also work with customers looking for discontinued or difficult-to-source parts.

For procurement teams, I think the more interesting question is not simply “Where can I buy this part?”, but:

How do you balance availability, authenticity, lead time, price, and supply-chain risk when sourcing hard-to-find components?

I'd be interested to hear how others in the semiconductor industry approach this problem, especially for production-critical components.
